overall_reason: The hero picture is a skeleton dashboard of six unlabelled purple gradient bars, and the rest of the imagery is the generated-page kit: emoji feature icons in tinted tiles, a sparkle 'Powered by AI' pill, a gradient CTA band and a grey text logo row of placeholder names.

score.reason: T-ILLUSTRATION-READ and T-DELETE-PICTURE fail on the empty hero dashboard, and T-AI-LOOK, T-TREATMENT, T-ICON-SYSTEM and T-LOGO-ROW fail on the emoji icons, purple gradients and the text logo row (IMG-007, IMG-012, IMG-013, IMG-014).

findings.title: A product illustration is built to be read
findings.where: hero, below the CTAs, about x 181 to 1100 and y 530 to 860 of the 1280 image
findings.evidence: The hero's product picture, about 920 by 330px and the largest picture on the page, is a window with grey skeleton bars where the sidebar and title would be and six purple-to-violet gradient bars with no axis, labels, values or dates. Removing it leaves the hero's message unchanged (T-DELETE-PICTURE).
findings.before: A skeleton dashboard with six unlabelled gradient bars.
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: a capture of a real Cadence chart, for example a funnel or retention view with its labels and numbers, at 2x]
findings.why: An analytics product's lead picture is its one chance to show an answer; a chart with no labels shows no answer and reads as a template filler (IMG-003 as well).

findings.title: One icon system
findings.where: feature cards, about y 1310 to 1370 of the 1280 image; 'Powered by AI' pill at y 172; footer, bottom right at y 3120
findings.evidence: The three feature cards use colour emoji (a bar chart, a lightning bolt and a rocket) inside pale tinted tiles, the hero pill opens with a sparkle emoji, and the footer's three social links are small colour emoji-style glyphs. These are three unrelated drawing styles, and none is a drawn icon set. Sweep rules SLP-013 (emoji icons), SLP-003 (icon tile) and SLP-015 (AI sparkle) cover the same marks; their hits were not captured for this item.
findings.before: Emoji in tinted tiles, a sparkle emoji, and emoji-style social glyphs.
findings.after: One stroke icon set at one weight (for example 1.5px at 20px) for the three features, no sparkle, and the owners' own one-colour marks or plain text labels for the social links.
findings.why: Emoji render differently on every platform and carry no meaning specific to the feature; the sparkle and rocket are the generated-page kit's default marks (IMG-001).

findings.title: Treatment and texture come from the brand
findings.where: hero headline 'just works', hero bars and glow, stat figures, CTA band at about y 2530 to 2812 of the 1280 image
findings.evidence: One indigo-to-violet-to-pink gradient is applied to the headline words 'just works', the six hero bars, the four stat figures, the primary buttons and the full-width 'Ready to get started?' band, and a violet glow spreads under the hero window. No brand authority names this treatment. Sweep rules SLP-007 (gradient), SLP-008 (glow) and the neon_violet detector's hits were not captured for this item.
findings.before: A purple gradient and violet glow on text, bars, buttons and the CTA band.
findings.after: One flat brand colour for the primary action, solid bars in the chart, and the CTA band on a flat surface with no glow under the hero frame.
findings.why: The same gradient on every element is the generated-page default and removes the one cue that would mark the primary action.
findings.root: one gradient token used across components

findings.title: Logos are the owners' marks at even weight
findings.where: 'Trusted by fast-moving teams at' row, about y 1010 of the 1280 image
findings.evidence: The logo row sets six names (Northwind, Lumen, Vertex, Quanta, Beacon, Atlas) as grey bold text in the page font, not as marks. Northwind is a well-known sample-company name. Whether these customers exist belongs to SLP-016 and INT-010 (lens-integrity); this lens notes only that no owner's mark is shown.
findings.before: Six placeholder names typed in the page font.
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: the real customers' one-colour marks at one optical height], or remove the row until real customers agree to appear.
findings.why: A text row in one font shows that no real marks were supplied; it reads as a template slot.

strengths: Nothing qualifies as real material; the only consistent element is the purple diamond logo, which is used the same way in the header and footer.
not_investigated: image-only item: natural sizes, hosts, file names, alt text, density, crops at 375 and the sweep's per-element hits (fake_people, img_alt, mixed_icons, emoji_icons, icon_tile, gradient, glow, performance) were not captured; T-IMAGE-SIZE and T-CROP-375 were judged only from what the one image shows
the whole artifact is one screenshot, so it is one sample; confidence is medium at most
licences and credits: the capture cannot see licences
menus, carousels, tabs, hover states and lazy content: no interaction was captured
art direction at other widths: only one width exists
T-CAPTURE-READ: no product capture; the hero window is an illustration, judged with T-ILLUSTRATION-READ (C48)
T-TEXT-ON-IMAGE: no text over a picture
the invented customer names and the 12,000+, 8B, 4.9 and 99.99% figures belong to lens-integrity (INT-010, SLP-016)
